C_identical_key_sets.fails_if: pathmap and the Python trie disagree on how many keys they loaded -- the comparison would be between different inputs
C_identical_key_sets.can_fail: either pathmap keys count differs from the dumped count

C_probe_reads_pathmap_correctly.fails_if: pathmap's own 8-path test set does not give 6 nodes through this probe -- then the probe is misreading the library and the verdict is VOID, not negative
C_probe_reads_pathmap_correctly.can_fail: the tiny set reports any node count other than 6

C_falsifier_fires_on_atoms.fails_if: the mean node-depth ratio on atom keys is under 10.0x -- the falsifier would NOT fire and S73/S74's proof sizes would transfer to real pathmap
C_falsifier_fires_on_atoms.can_fail: depth_ratio_mean for atoms reads below the threshold

C_falsifier_does_not_fire_on_triples.fails_if: fixed-length triple keys ALSO exceed the threshold -- then the cause is not key length and the mechanism claimed here is wrong
C_falsifier_does_not_fire_on_triples.can_fail: depth_ratio_mean for triples reads above the threshold

C_merkleize_is_deterministic.fails_if: pathmap's merkleize hash changes between two runs on the same trie -- it would not be content-derived

C_merkleize_is_dedup_not_commitment.fails_if: pathmap depends on any cryptographic hash -- then it can emit a real commitment and W2 may have reimplemented something that existed
C_merkleize_is_dedup_not_commitment.can_fail: a sha2/sha3/blake3/keccak/digest dependency appears in pathmap Cargo.toml

observed.hash_is_gxhash_declared_for: for dag_serialization, merkleization, and caching catamorphism
observed.name_grep_was_a_false_positive: fn witness in pathmap is a Rust borrow token (-> Self::WitnessT, several -> ()), not a proof

C_dedup_actually_reuses.fails_if: merkleize reuses no nodes on either corpus -- the structural sharing S73's cost model leans on would be absent here
C_dedup_actually_reuses.can_fail: reused reads 0 for atoms or for triples
